readerNotes.text: paper-meme joined the public suite on 22 October as a Robinhood Chain paper book. Its daily screening list is the public Fund OS screen that $SHUFFLE, a meme index on Robinhood Chain, now uses for its token universe. Anyone can inspect the daily candidates on the fund screening page. Screens still stop at ideas: council and execution decide size, venue, and fills on live books.

body: This week's public micro books use Guru Lotus and Lagoon custody adapters, plus one paper book. base04, base05, and base06 sit on Guru Lotus vaults on Base. Messy's engine runs research, council decisioning, and trade construction; capital on those books sits in Guru's vault contracts. On the Guru books, the trading key can trade but cannot withdraw, a limit enforced by the vault contracts, not our software. lg-base00, lg-base01, and lg-base02 sit on Lagoon vaults on Base. safe-lg-rh01 sits on a Lagoon vault on Robinhood Chain. paper-meme is a paper-trading book on Robinhood Chain used for public screening proof; it does not hold live capital in a vault adapter. Provider-side contract failure is venue risk on the live adapters. Keys for live books live in Turnkey; our backend never holds key material.

suiteIntro: Weekly workflow proof for Messy-managed micro test funds on Base and Robinhood Chain: Guru Lotus books base04, base05, and base06, plus Lagoon books lg-base00, lg-base01, lg-base02, and safe-lg-rh01, plus paper book paper-meme. Screening prepares evidence; the Chair decides; the system records the resolution; only then can execution mutate the book. Macro and narrative below are the postures those sessions used, not a live market refresh at publish time.
